# Production Warehouse

> A catalog of about 800 motion-design videos with the prompts that made them, and 44 written motion-design techniques with worked demos. Public, read-only, no sign-in.

## For AI clients

- MCP server (Streamable HTTP, read-only): https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/mcp . Tools: search_videos, get_video, get_video_doc, list_filters, list_techniques, get_technique, search_techniques.
- Video catalog as JSON: https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/items.json (one object per video: title, author, category, tags, prompt, links to videos and poster).
- Techniques and skills as JSON with markdown bodies: https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/techniques.json
- Local MCP over stdio: the mcp/ folder of https://github.com/suenot/mvw-viewer

## Pages

- [Technique: line boil, a contour that is redrawn while the shape stays still](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/line-boil): Redraw each outline a dozen times a second with a little wobble, so a still pose looks hand-drawn. How it works, a small code recipe and where it goes wrong.
- [Technique: drawing cadence and a stable seed](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/cadence-and-seed): Why the redraw rhythm must come from time, not from the frame number, and why the random numbers must be seeded so a re-render gives the same picture.
- [Technique: hatching instead of a flat fill](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/hatching): Shade with strokes, not with a solid colour. A circle-and-chord recipe, a second crossing pass and the reasons it keeps a drawing from looking digital.
- [Technique: construction lines and broken strokes](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/construction-lines): Leave the artist's scaffolding in the picture: faint guides under the contour, and a contour made of short strokes with gaps.
- [Technique: a timing plan as editable data](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/timing-plan): Write when every object enters, moves and leaves as plain numbers on one timeline, so a late correction is one edit, not a new render of everything.
- [Technique: a style contract (style DNA) before any scene](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/style-contract): Turn style words into numbers (line weight, wobble, palette, cadence) and hand them to every scene, so ten shapes look like one set.
- [Technique: render, then inspect real frames](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/render-and-inspect): A quality gate that cannot be argued with: pull frames at fixed times from an actual render, write down what is wrong with each, fix the source.
- [Motion techniques Claude can use](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques): Forty-four motion-design techniques from the studied tutorials, the prompt database, the owner's curves project, our own 3D work and a read-through of skill repositories, one article each with an animated demo of how it works.
- [Technique: an error log that turns into checks](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/error-log): Keep a short list of concrete failures and the rule each one produced, so the next scene starts stronger without a longer prompt.
- [Motion skills: where to extract the techniques](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/skills): The skills and repositories behind the motion techniques, with licences, what each one yields and the verdict from our trial, plus a procedure for extracting a technique safely.
- [Technique: build long work from short approved pieces](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/assemble-from-pieces): Make and approve one short scene at a time, then join them and review only the seams.
- [Use the warehouse from an AI: MCP and JSON](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/ai): Connect an AI assistant to the catalog of motion videos and prompts and to the technique articles through a read-only MCP server, or read the same data as plain JSON.
- [Technique: painted layers, with light and text in code](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/layered-assets): Generate the detailed pictures as separate transparent layers, then let code do depth, light, particles and text. Parallax is the proof it works.
- [Technique: one sentence, one shot, cut just before the word](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/sentence-shot): Cut to a new picture a fraction of a second before its sentence begins, and put the longest pause before the punch line. Measured from a 30 s demo.
- [Technique: a number as a readout, not a slam](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/number-readout): Show a figure small, beside the thing it measures, on the spoken word, with a thin measuring line. It reads as evidence, not as decoration.
- [Technique: a seekable frame function](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/seekable-frame): Write the whole picture as renderAt(t), a pure function of time, so any moment can be frozen, checked and re-rendered exactly.
- [Technique: closed-form springs](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/closed-form-springs): Move things with the exact step response of a spring, a formula of time, and give the camera a slower spring than the shape.
- [Technique: a beat grid](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/beat-grid): Put every move, click and sound on a fixed grid of beats so a piece without a soundtrack still feels in time, and music can be added later.
- [Technique: a seamless loop](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/seamless-loop): Make the last frame equal the first, including the cursor, so a piece can repeat with no visible seam.
- [Technique: motion blur from subframes](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/subframe-blur): Draw four samples inside each frame and blend them, so fast movement gets a short streak instead of a sharp hop.
- [Technique: one shape, never cut](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/one-shape): Tell a product story with one element that morphs from state to state, driven by a cursor, with no cuts and no cross-fades.
- [Technique: kinetic type per glyph](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/kinetic-type): Treat every letter as its own element with its own spring and a fixed stagger, so words arrive as a rhythm and not as a block.
- [Technique: a reveal through the letters](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/mask-reveal): Replace one line of text with the next by turning the outgoing word into a window, so the cut is made by the type itself.
- [Technique: print misregistration](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/misregistration): Show two offset colour copies of text for a moment on impact frames only, like a badly aligned print.
- [Technique: a storyboard before code, stills before render](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/storyboard-first): Show a beat-by-beat storyboard before any code, and render one still per beat before the full render, so problems are found cheaply.
- [Technique: reference by link](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/reference-by-link): Give the assistant a link to a clip you like and ask for your own story in that style, instead of describing the style in words.
- [Technique: feedback in passes](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/feedback-passes): Improve a coded video in short passes, one concern at a time: pace, then sound, then music fitted to the beat.
- [Technique: a locked message and a ban list](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/locked-message): Fix the exact words and their order, and list what must not appear, so the model spends its effort on motion and not on inventing copy.
- [Technique: shapes as harmonics, and morphing between them](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/harmonic-morph): Store a closed outline as a few complex harmonics, then morph between two outlines by mixing coefficients. The same list is also a smoothness dial.
- [Technique: letters as compound harmonic contours](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/harmonic-type): A glyph is a few closed contours. Fill them as one compound path with the even-odd rule so holes stay open, and draw text from the same primitives as the art.
- [Technique: a contour spectrum as a voice](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/shape-to-sound): Use the magnitudes of a shape's harmonics as the partials of a tone, so the look of a character sets its timbre. All sound is synthesised, so it is deterministic.
- [Technique: a clock per motion, accumulated](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/independent-clocks): Change a speed without moving the past: advance each motion's own phase by speed times dt, and give every motion its own clock.
- [Technique: a camera that is a curve of time](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/camera-curves): Give a 3D camera a few channels, key each one, and join the keys with monotone Hermite curves: smooth, no overshoot, flat on holds, and a pure function of time.
- [Technique: a sharp band that makes a scene look small](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/tilt-shift): Blur everything except one horizontal band and a real scene reads as a miniature. Key the band like a camera channel, and seed any grain by frame number.
- [Technique: a Blender animation as frame numbers](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/blender-frames): Script Blender without its interface, key a scene, and render every frame from its number. We ran a small test and measured what comes out.
- [Technique: motion defaults in frames](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/motion-defaults): When nobody says how long a move lasts, use measured medians: opacity 6 frames, entrances 12, blur 7, exits 10 to 13, at 30 fps.
- [Technique: an importance budget](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/importance-budget): Rate every beat 1, 2 or 3 and give level 3 to at most a quarter of them, so the biggest moves still mean something.
- [Technique: a speed ramp as a time remap](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/speed-ramp): Slow down into an impact and snap back: speed is a curve, the source frame is its running sum, and the slowest frame lands on the beat.
- [Technique: cuts on the downbeat, without a startle](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/downbeat-cuts): Give each scene a whole number of bars so every cut lands on a downbeat, and mark the cut with a chord change, not with volume.
- [Technique: three B-roll treatments and per-beat timing](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/broll-treatments): Mark each line of a talking-head clip as speaker, overlay or cover, then decide per element whether it leads, syncs or waits for the word.
- [Technique: a lower third that stays inside the safe area](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/lower-third): A name strap in the bottom third: inside title-safe, motion only in the build-in and build-out, and a hold that stands still while it is read.
- [Technique: a hand that draws on, tip on the point](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/hand-draw-on): A whiteboard draw-on: one eased value draws the stroke, and the pen sits on the point at that same value; between strokes it lifts and moves unseen.
- [Technique: reveal a diagram in order](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/progressive-diagram): Nodes first, then edges, then labels; then keep the active node at full strength and dim the rest to 35 percent.
- [Technique: gradients in OKLCH](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/oklch-gradients): Blend two colours in OKLCH instead of sRGB numbers and the middle of the gradient keeps its chroma instead of going grey.
- [Technique: parallax from three layer speeds](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/parallax-layers): Move the background at 0.2x, the midground at 0.6x and the foreground at 1.2x, so depth is read from the speed difference.
- [Technique: reduced motion in three tiers](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/reduced-motion-tiers): When a viewer asks for less motion, remove the vestibular triggers, shorten the rest to a fade, and keep colour changes and progress.
- [Technique: the vertical safe box](https://production-warehouse.suenot.com/#/techniques/vertical-safe-box): In a 1080 by 1920 short, keep the hook and the key subject in the centre 900 by 1400 box and the bottom 320 px clear of text.
